title: Inline prompt debugging - personal PRD sketch
body:
Quick brain dump for an "inline prompt debugger" feature (console + SDK). Purpose: let engineers iterate on prompts and prompt-related runtime behavior inside Redwood without spinning up prod traffic or writing custom harnesses.

Problem statement:
- Engineers spend hours reproducing odd outputs locally and in prod; debugging involves ad-hoc scripts, logging, and rerunning with different batching/kv/cache settings.
- Missing visibility: token-level timing, which cached prefixes were hit, what model variant used for fallback, how function-calling resolved.

Core idea / capabilities (MVP):
1) Prompt replay sandbox: paste prompt + metadata (model, temperature, system) and replay with deterministic seeds. Show full request/response.
2) Token timeline view: token-by-token timings, token costs, and which kernel/batch was used (simulated).
3) KV cache inspector: show what prefix is cached, approximate memory impact, ability to toggle cache-on/cache-off to compare outputs and latency.
4) Batching simulator: take a set of incoming prompts (upload a small CSV) and visualize batching impact on latency and cost; preview recommended batch sizes.
5) Function-call trace: if functions used, show call sequence, args, and whether Redwood's structured output parsing altered the result.
6) Cost/latency estimator: approximate per-request delta for quantization, shorter context, or enabling prefix cache.
7) Save/compare runs: users can save named runs and diff outputs to spot regressions.

User stories:
- As an engineer, I want to see why a specific prompt flips between answers when different batch sizes are used, so I can choose a stable config.
- As an SRE, I want to simulate 1000 concurrent prompts with current batching settings to estimate 95th percentile latency.
- As a support engineer, I want to replay a customer bug with the exact model and prompt used, including the same KV/cache state.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console has a sandbox panel that accepts prompt + config and returns the simulated run within 10s for small inputs.
- Token timeline visual exists and exposes token cost and timing per token.
- Users can toggle cache to see different latencies and outputs.
- Runs can be saved and compared in a lightweight diff view.

UX notes / sketches (text):
- Left column: request builder (model, temperature, system, functions, file upload for prompt set).
- Middle: response view with token timeline under it (click token => shows latency + kernel).
- Right panel: run metadata (est cost, cache hits, batch simulation results).
- Top bar: run name, save, compare, export request as SDK snippet.

Open questions / risks:
- How deterministic can we reasonably be when simulating fallback routing and dedicated vs hosted variants? Need a simulated policy engine or snapshot of routing rules.
- Security: if users paste customer PII in prompts, retention and export controls needed; default to ephemeral runs with TTL.
- Infrastructure cost: replaying many runs could consume GPU cycles. Need quota and cheap-mode (small token limit / quantized simulation).
- Ties to private deployments: will private customers want this locally? Could ship a lightweight agent for on-prem replay.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE for safe sandbox resource limits (todo: ping @noah).
- Mock up console UI (low-fi) and run usability test with 3 internal engineers.
- Write a tiny SDK prototype that can capture exact request metadata and replay it via hosted API.
- Draft a proposal for ephemeral retention policy + opt-in export.

Notes to self:
- Keep MVP focused: token timeline + cache toggle + save/compare. Batching simulator could be alpha-level.
- Check reuse: can we reuse existing tracing infra from observability team? Link: CONFLUENCE_TRACING_PROPOSAL (placeholder).

Random low-priority ideas (parking lot):
- Integrate with change-runs for rollouts (run A/B of two prompt fixes across a small percentage of traffic).
- Autotune suggestions: detect patterns where small prompt edits reduce tokens/cost and suggest edits.
- Chatty mode: annotate model hallucinations inline with likely cause (missing KB, temperature).

Rough timeline (personal):
- Week 0-2: prototype SDK + minimal console form.
- Week 3-4: add token timeline and cache toggle.
- Week 5: internal dogfood + iterate.

Action items (who/when):
- Alex: prototype SDK and console form (due 2026-01-29).
- Maya: coordinate usability session (due 2026-02-05).
- Noah: SRE limits + quoting infra cost (due 2026-02-12).

End of scratchpad. Keep messy.
